gen-gf-gabarito-gf-commissioner: Commissioner reads smoothly, its curves never clogging and every stroke held to a single thickness. Gabarito, though, brings the flair, its open-cut terminals letting each counter flow outward, while Commissioner just keeps the line moving.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-doto: Doto leaves wide margins of space around each glyph, with generous mouths on the round letters. And across paragraphs, that spacing should feel easygoing, while Gabarito's letterforms look bent from one length of tubing.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-exo: Neon-glass thickness from a one-nib hand: that's the Gabarito look. Exo keeps clean, wide gaps between its letters, so tiny sizes stay crisp and whole paragraphs go down easily.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-exo-2: Gabarito draws with a constant-width pen line, its counters flowing outward for a look that is expressive and distinctive. Exo 2 has plenty of daylight inside its curves, so paragraphs feel clean and unhurried.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-faculty-glyphic: One nib, no thick or thin, not even in the w: that is Gabarito. And Faculty Glyphic keeps its rounded letters clearly open, so text reads modern and uncrowded.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-gowun-dodum: Expressive and distinctive, Gabarito looks drawn with one nib, its counters flowing outward. Gowun Dodum settles in underneath with a wide-mouthed lowercase a and smooth, tube-like lines, so the two sit together without fighting.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-gudea: Gudea draws thread-like curves, leaving glass-clear gaps where each terminal meets its stroke. And what stands out is Gabarito's expressive, open-cut counters flowing outward against that fine, approachable text.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-hubot-sans: Gabarito draws monoline strokes throughout, with open terminals that let its counters flow outward. And Hubot Sans, with its widely opened e, keeps the text contemporary and modern beneath it.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-ibm-plex-sans-devanag: Gabarito's steady, marker-like line weight gives it an expressive hand. IBM Plex Sans Devanagari adds rope-loose curves that never knot at the ends, giving the text a modern ease.
gen-gf-gabarito-gf-k2d: One nib, open counters, plenty of attitude: that's Gabarito at the top. And K2D keeps a tube-like thickness through every bend, its c terminals hanging far from the bowl, so text moves along smoothly.
